sources.name: Advanced Construction Robotics — TyBOT specifications revision C
Advanced Construction Robotics — TyBOT brochure revision D
Advanced Construction Robotics — TyBOT product and supervisor workflow

highlights: Gantry robot locates and ties horizontal rebar intersections on bridge decks
Operates on project edge forms or screed rails without pre-mapping or BIM input
Expandable working width supports different deck layouts; crews handle remaining installation tasks
Revision C specifies 900 ties/hour minimum and 1200-plus observed active tying. These ratings exclude a guarantee for downtime, wire changes or an entire shift.

The 1864 kg mass belongs to the base unit. Truss end-to-end widths of 9.5/20.5/38.5 m remain separate from the 10-117 ft adjustable rail span; named size settings do not create additional robot models.

The generator is rated for up to ten hours without refueling. The brochure’s 12-plus-hour Belly Box battery powers the supervisor interface, and optional one-ton carry hoists do not establish standard robot payload.

Tie patterns cover all, alternate or every third intersection. Rail travel is rated at 0.2 m/s; bar spacing, rail support and span-dependent grade limits constrain installation. Rain-or-shine marketing is not a numeric ingress rating.

sources.name: Advanced Construction Robotics — IronBOT V3.0 specifications
Advanced Construction Robotics — IronBOT family product and placement workflow

highlights: The manufacturer PDF explicitly identifies IronBOT V3.0. Its placement boom has a 5000 lb/2267.96 kg bundle capacity, handling 9-60 ft bars; capacity is separate from the family page’s 5000 lb/hour placement claim.
Rail span adjusts from 27 to 117 ft. The sheet lists 0.2 m/s travel and 50-plus hours of generator endurance, rather than battery operation; bar length and rail span are different dimensions.
The sheet pairs 21000-31000 lb unloaded with 10000-14000 kg, and 11-15 ft height with 3.43-4.77 m. Conversions disagree, so both unresolved ranges remain visible.

The current family workflow requires a supervisor to establish the first position and spacing and assist singulation. Local odometry governs subsequent placement; rain-or-shine and schedule-savings claims are not an ingress certificate or guaranteed project outcome.

companyFocus.name: Advanced Construction Robotics
companyFocus.role: Bridge-deck rebar tying and material placement robots with supervisor and reporting workflows
highlights: TyBOT ties rebar intersections and IronBOT handles rebar placement. Gantry widths, carry accessories and the combined installation offering are configurations or services, not additional independently identified robot models.

The BOTs platform reports tie counts, active hours, equipment utilization and faults. These reporting and support functions are software services, separate from physical robot models and independently tested productivity.

Manufacturer workflows retain human supervisors and crews for wire changes, initial positioning, singulation and remaining installation tasks. RaaS and Certified Innovator offers do not establish universal pricing, local stock or guaranteed schedule savings.
